title: Canada-US Trade Dispute Boosts Maple Syrup Sales
paragraphs: Maple syrup has long been one of Canada's most famous products — and people around the world are buying more of it. In fact, Canadian maple syrup exports were worth about $607 million in 2025, an increase of 17% from the year before.
This is good news for Canadian maple syrup companies like Hutchinson Acres, which says even now it's getting more international orders than usual.
One reason for this increase in exports may be the ongoing trade dispute between Canada and the US.
In February 2025, not long after coming back into office, US President Donald Trump announced tariffs on a number of Canadian products.

And despite signs of progress, in August this year, trade talks between the two countries collapsed, with both sides putting new tariffs on one another's products. America also banned a number of Canadian products, while most Canadian provinces have banned the sale of US alcohol since 2025.
Canada produces over 75% of the world's maple syrup, while the US makes about 25%.

Speaking to CBC News, Hutchinson Acres co-owner Chris Hutchinson said his sales often go up when Canada-US trade disputes are in the news — and it's not just because Canadians want to be extra-sure to buy from Canadian businesses.

Europeans have also been upset by US tariffs and what they see as bad trade deals that have been made to try to reduce them. And Philippe Coley, whose company sells maple syrup in Europe, said more people there now care about which country their syrup comes from — and they want to be sure it's from Canada.

However, politics isn't the only reason international customers are buying more maple syrup — some are also using it instead of processed sugars. In Saudi Arabia, for example, Hutchinson says some customers are adding maple syrup to their coffee.
